verdicts.title: Topological classification of quasitoric manifolds with the second Betti number 2
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: A quasitoric manifold is a $2n$-dimensional compact smooth manifold with a locally standard action of an $n$-dimensional torus whose orbit space is a simple polytope. In this article, we classify quasitoric manifolds with the second Betti number $β_2=2$ topologically. Interestingly, they are distinguished by their cohomology rings up to homeomorphism.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns topological classification of quasitoric manifolds with second Betti number 2, with no mention of d-regular graphs, communication complexity, or rank variance bounds. It shares only the vocabulary 'second Betti number' with the conjecture.

verdicts.title: A bound on the second Betti number of hyperkähler manifolds of complex dimension six
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: Let M be an irreducible compact hyperkähler manifold of complex dimension six. Under an assumption on the Looijenga-Lunts-Verbitsky decomposition of the cohomology of M, we prove that the second Betti number of M is at most 23.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract bounds the second Betti number of hyperkähler manifolds of complex dimension six (≤23), which shares the term 'second Betti number' but concerns differential geometry of hyperkähler manifolds, not graphs, communication complexity, or rank variance.

verdicts.title: A conjectural bound on the second Betti number for hyper-Kähler manifolds
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In previous work, we noted that the known cases of hyper-Kähler manifolds satisfy a natural condition on the LLV decomposition of the cohomology; informally, the Verbitsky component is the dominant representation in the LLV decomposition. Assuming this condition holds for all hyper-Kähler manifolds, we obtain an upper bound for the second Betti number in terms of the dimension.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns bounds on the second Betti number for hyper-Kähler manifolds via LLV decomposition, sharing only the term 'second Betti number' with the conjecture but having no interaction with d-regular graphs or communication complexity rank variance.
